title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
Tesla told a family that data from a fatal Autopilot crash had been deleted from their vehicle, making investigation impossible. A hacker later demonstrated that Tesla vehicles retain this crash data, contradicting the company's claim. This represents a system deployed without adequate checks on what information was actually recoverable or what claims about it were accurate.

The failure occurred at the point of evidence handling and disclosure in a fatal crash investigation. Tesla asserted as fact that data was unavailable when it was not, a claim that went unchecked until independent verification revealed it to be false. A jury found Tesla liable and ordered damages of more than $240 million, a verdict a judge later upheld.

It is not established why Tesla made the claim about missing data or what internal processes led to it.
